title: My purpose Talents and abilities
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The child narrates Matthew 25:14-30 (five, two and one talents; two servants double theirs, one buries his) and says the lesson: use the gifts God gives, however many, faithfully.

floor.prerequisite: Knows each person is God's special creation.
floor.question: What does Psalm 139:14 say about how you are made?

representations: a chart: given, gained, what the master said
steps: The faithful are praised; the one who hid his is blamed.
contexts: a child who sings in the choir
a learner good at drawing who helps make class charts
a farmer who uses a small plot well

board.do: Wait for the child to say he hid it and did not use it.
Fill in the chart and write "use your gifts".

listen_for: Keep your money safe and never spend it
misconceptions.ask: What does the parable of the talents teach a Grade 5 learner?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what the servants did with what they were given. Then name other gifts: singing, kindness, farming, drawing, helping.

listen_for: He was given less than the others
misconceptions.ask: Why was the third servant blamed?
misconceptions.repair: Reread Matthew 25:15, "each according to his ability", then the servant's own words about fear and the buried talent.

misconceptions.ask: How many talents did the first servant gain?
misconceptions.repair: Draw three columns: given, gained, total. Fill them from Matthew 25:16-18.

listen_for: Less praise, because he gained less
misconceptions.ask: What did the master say to the servant who gained two more talents (Matthew 25:23)?
misconceptions.repair: Read 25:21 and 25:23 side by side: the same words. The master praised faithfulness, not the size.

checks.question: How many more talents did the servant with five gain?
What does the parable teach?
checks.answer: Use the gifts God gives you

skills.key_step: The child says what the three verses teach: God has plans for a hope and a future (Jeremiah 29:11), every good gift comes from God (James 1:17), and each gift is for serving others (1 Peter 4:10).

floor.prerequisite: Knows God is a loving Father.
floor.question: Which verse says "God is love"?

representations: three verse cards with a key word each: plans, gift, serve
a gift box drawn on the board
steps: Read James 1:17: good gifts from God.
Read 1 Peter 4:10: use gifts to serve.
Name a gift and how it serves others.
contexts: a child good at football who coaches younger ones
a learner who reads to a blind grandparent

board.do: Draw a gift box and write James 1:17 on it.

board.say: Who gives every good gift? What is it for?

board.do: Wait for the child to say God, to serve others.

listen_for: Show it off so others admire you
misconceptions.ask: According to 1 Peter 4:10, what should each person do with the gift received?
misconceptions.repair: Read 1 Peter 4:10 aloud and ask who benefits when a gift is used to serve.

listen_for: God has plans only for adults
misconceptions.ask: What does Jeremiah 29:11 say about God's plans?
misconceptions.repair: Read Jeremiah 29:11 and ask who God is speaking about. Say that a Grade 5 child is included.

listen_for: From a person's own hard work alone
misconceptions.ask: According to James 1:17, where does every good gift come from?
misconceptions.repair: Read James 1:17. Say that work matters, but that the ability to work and learn is a gift too.

listen_for: No, God's plan will happen anyway
misconceptions.ask: If God has a plan for you (Jeremiah 29:11), should you still work hard at school?
misconceptions.repair: Join Jeremiah 29:11 with 1 Peter 4:10: God gives the hope; we use the gifts.

checks.question: Where does every good gift come from, according to James 1:17?
What does 1 Peter 4:10 say to do with a gift?
